home-assistant.name: Home Assistant add-on
home-assistant.title: Install xomtra as a Home Assistant add-on
home-assistant.desc: Step-by-step installation of the xomtra add-on for Home Assistant OS: requirements, add-on repository, first token, connecting Claude and backups.
home-assistant.lead: The add-on runs xomtra next to Home Assistant in one container. No domain, no port forwarding and no cloud account; Claude Desktop and Claude Code connect over your home network.

ul: Home Assistant OS or Supervised. Only installations with the Supervisor have add-ons. With Home Assistant Container or Core, use Docker Compose instead.
SSD, at least 4 GB RAM and 20 GB of free space. Home Assistant Green (32 GB eMMC) and SD cards are not supported.
64-bit system: amd64 (Intel, AMD) or aarch64 (for example Raspberry Pi 5 with an SSD).

b.note: Do you want to keep state history for more than a year, or back up the whole history? Run xomtra on its own machine with Docker Compose; Proxmox and VMware images are coming soon.

b: In Home Assistant open Settings → Add-ons → Add-on Store, then the three-dot menu → Repositories. Paste this address and select Add:
Reload the store, open xomtra and select Install. The Supervisor pulls the signed image for your system. Keep Start on boot and Watchdog on and select Start.

The first start creates the add-on's database and all internal keys in its own data folder; it takes about a minute. Nobody has to type a password. Then xomtra starts loading the history Home Assistant still keeps, in the background.
MCP clients reach xomtra on port 8000 of your Home Assistant host. On the Configuration tab, set mcp_url to the address your computers use for Home Assistant, for example:

This setting is optional: without it the admin page uses the host you opened Home Assistant on. It is shown with every new token, so set it once and the instructions are always right. Save and restart the add-on.
Open xomtra in the sidebar (only Home Assistant administrators see it) and go to Tokens. Fill in who the token is for, the device or app, the role and the expiry:

ul: xomtra.Reader reads the history and findings, without presence, locations, cameras and locks. Right for most people.
xomtra.Admin sees every entity, including those, and the drift of the catalog.

b: The token (xmt_…) is shown once. Issue one per person and device: you can revoke one without the others, and the audit shows who asked what.
Claude Desktop: on Connect clients, download the extension xomtra.mcpb (the address is already filled in), open it and paste the token.
Claude Code:
Any other MCP client that speaks Streamable HTTP and can send an Authorization header works the same way. Then ask your first question, for example “Which sensors stopped reporting this week?”

b.note: Claude on the web and in the phone apps connects from Anthropic's servers and cannot reach your home network. Use Claude Desktop or Claude Code on a computer at home or connected by your VPN.

b: On the admin page Answers you choose the guardrails for your assistant's answers. The set Default looks for the relevant data first, gives the answer first and then the evidence as a chart or a table, in a friendly tone. Concise answers as briefly as possible, and you can duplicate any set and write your own. A fixed core always applies on top of every set: only values fetched from xomtra, no conclusions about a person's presence, sleep or health unless you ask, and no jokes about accidents or threats to life and health. A change applies within 30 seconds, without a restart.

Home Assistant backups keep xomtra's tokens, settings, answer sets and dismissed findings, but not the lake with the history (tens of GB). After a restore xomtra starts a new lake, loads the history again as far back as Home Assistant still keeps it, and computes the findings again.
New versions appear in Home Assistant as add-on updates. Read the release notes before updating: before version 1.0 a minor release may change settings.

docker.name: Docker Compose
docker.title: Install xomtra with Docker Compose
docker.desc: Step-by-step installation of xomtra on your own Linux server with Docker Compose: verified release, start with one command, connecting Home Assistant in the browser, first token, connecting Claude, upgrades and uninstalling.
docker.lead: For Home Assistant Container or Core, or when you want xomtra on its own Linux server. xomtra reads Home Assistant over your network; Claude Desktop and Claude Code connect with personal tokens, only from your LAN.

ul: Linux with Docker Engine and Compose v2, amd64 (Intel, AMD; the images are not built for arm64 yet). Install it by the official guide and check it with docker compose version.

SSD, at least 4 GB RAM (8 GB recommended) and 20 GB of free space for a typical home; more for years of state history. The Docker installation runs the full xomtra stack and is meant for a machine with enough memory, not for a small server; on a small machine use the Home Assistant add-on.
Home Assistant reachable from this machine, usually on port 8123 (URL like http://<address>:8123).

b: If curl is missing:
Find the latest version, download it and the release's checksums and pinned image references:
Check the downloaded files against SHA256SUMS; every line must end with OK:
Unpack the release (the directory xomtra/deploy/compose of its tag) and go into it:

b.note: Optional: you can also check that every image was signed by the release workflow of this version, with cosign in its container; see the documentation.

b: There are no passwords to fill in: xomtra generates its internal passwords and keys itself on the first start. The only file you create is .env with the pinned images:

Optional: to reach xomtra under a name instead of its LAN address, add the name now, before the first start. It only has to resolve to this server on your own computers (for example a DNS record in your router); no public DNS is needed. You can change it later and then run docker compose up -d --force-recreate.

On the first start the one-time service secrets-init generates every internal password and key into the Docker volume secrets and finds this server's address in your LAN; xomtra is then at https://<server>/. All services should be running or healthy within a few minutes.

steps.h: Create a Home Assistant user for xomtra
b: In Home Assistant create a dedicated user without administrator rights, sign in as that user and create a long-lived access token on Profile → Security. Home Assistant has no read-only tokens, so this user could still control devices; xomtra only reads registries, history and statistics and never calls services. A separate user lets you revoke xomtra's access any time without touching your own account.
Until Home Assistant is connected, this command prints a one-time setup link (it is also in the log of the admin service):

Open the link in a browser in your LAN (the browser warns about the certificate, which is expected; see the next step). Enter the Home Assistant URL as this server reaches it, for example http://192.168.1.10:8123, and the token from the previous step.

xomtra checks the connection before saving it and stores the token encrypted in its database, not in a file. The link then stops working and the history from Home Assistant loads in the background. You can change the URL or the token later on the admin page under Overview.

Caddy issues the certificate for your server from its own local certificate authority. Download it once from https://<server>/xomtra-ca.crt (the browser warns the first time, which is expected) and compare its fingerprint with the server:
On your computer, the downloaded file must show the same fingerprint:

Claude Desktop needs nothing here: the extension from the admin page carries the certificate. Claude Code needs it (and Claude Desktop with an extension from elsewhere than the admin page): unlike the browser it cannot click through the warning and stops with unable to get local issuer certificate. Start Claude Code with NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS=/path/to/xomtra-ca.crt (recommended, no change to the system), or trust the certificate for the whole computer:

steps.h: Issue a token and connect Claude
b: Open https://<server>/admin/, sign in as a Home Assistant administrator and go to Tokens. Issue one token per person and device (xomtra.Reader for most people); it is shown once.

Claude Desktop: after issuing the token, click Download for Claude Desktop (also on Connect clients), open xomtra.mcpb, paste the token and install. The file is made for your server: the address and the certificate are filled in and the extension trusts only this certificate, so nothing has to be imported into the computer. The token is not in the file, Claude Desktop keeps it as a secret.
Claude Code (if the certificate is not in your trust store, start Claude Code with NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS=/path/to/xomtra-ca.crt):

b.note: Claude on the web and in the phone apps connects from Anthropic's servers and cannot reach your LAN. For that, xomtra can run on a machine with a public https:// address, where you sign in with your Home Assistant account and two-factor authentication; see the documentation on GitHub.

b: On the admin page Answers you choose the guardrails for your assistant's answers. The set Default looks for the relevant data first, gives the answer first and then the evidence as a chart or a table, in a friendly tone. Concise answers as briefly as possible, and you can duplicate any set and write your own. A fixed core always applies on top of every set: only values fetched from xomtra, no conclusions about a person's presence, sleep or health unless you ask, and no jokes about accidents or threats to life and health. A change applies within 30 seconds, without a restart.
Read the release notes between your version and the new one first. Then, in xomtra/deploy/compose, set VERSION as in step 2 and run:
Pin the new images and restart:

Passwords and keys stay in the Docker volume secrets. An installation from before version 0.7.0 still has them in .env; the first start of the new version takes them over automatically, after which you can remove them from .env.

To roll back, unpack the archive of the previous version the same way, restore the .env backup and run docker compose up -d. Back up the machine or the Docker volumes regularly: they hold the whole history, and without the volume secrets the data cannot be read.

b.note: This cannot be undone. down -v deletes xomtra's whole copy of the history, its settings and issued tokens, the internal passwords and keys (volume secrets) and the server's certificate authority. Home Assistant keeps its own history. If you might come back, back up the volumes first.

b: Optional backup: in xomtra/deploy/compose stop xomtra and pack every volume into ~/xomtra-backup. The archive of secrets and the .env are secrets, keep them like a password:
Remove the containers, networks, volumes and images, check that no volume is left, delete the downloaded release and the unused image layers:

On your computers: in Claude Desktop remove the extension under Settings → Extensions → xomtra → Uninstall and delete xomtra.mcpb. Remove NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS from your shell profile if you set it. In Claude Code find the server by its address (you may have named it differently) and remove it by its name:

If you trusted the certificate for the whole computer, remove it (it is named xomtra local CA - <year> ECC Root; delete only this one) and delete xomtra-ca.crt. On Debian or Ubuntu delete the file in /usr/local/share/ca-certificates/ and run sudo update-ca-certificates --fresh.

In Home Assistant: sign in as the user for xomtra and delete its long-lived access token under Profile → Security; it stays valid until you do. Then delete that user under Settings → People. Sign-in with your own Home Assistant account leaves nothing behind. If you set up the public address for Claude on the web, also remove the connector in claude.ai, the port forward and the DNS record.
